prompt.context_jp: 夜更けの現像室では、モニターの淡い光だけ___人影を照らしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 夜更けの現像室では、モニターの淡い光だけ___人影を照らしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits after 「だけ」 here.

feedback.correct_en: だけが marks the exhaustive subject — only the monitor's faint light (nothing else) illuminated the figures. が highlights this as new, exhaustive information.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a topic and lose the 'only this one thing' exhaustive nuance. を would need a different verb frame; 照らしていた here takes a subject.

contrast_examples.en: As for light, it doesn't come in (topic/contrast).

prompt.context_jp: 呼び出しの目的を知らされていない武藤の眉___、わずかにひそめられていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 武藤の眉___、わずかにひそめられていた。

feedback.correct_en: は sets 武藤の眉 as the topic being described — the narrator comments on Mutou's brows as the known focus of attention.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it sound like newly-introduced information identifying what was furrowed, which doesn't match this descriptive, topical framing.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の眉はひそめられていた。

prompt.context_jp: 室内の空気___、名乗り合う前から張り詰めていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 室内の空気___、名乗り合う前から張り詰めていた。

feedback.correct_en: は marks 室内の空気 as the topic the narrator is describing — a scene-setting comment about what the atmosphere was like.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal new-information identification (what was tense), which doesn't fit a descriptive scene-setter.

prompt.context_jp: 「曽根さんのカルシウム密度___成人男性と同等だったということが分かりました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 曽根さんのカルシウム密度___成人男性と同等だった

feedback.correct_en: は sets Ms. Sone's calcium density as the topic being explained — 'as for her calcium density, it was equivalent to…'. This is a reporting/explaining frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as new-information subject, but An is announcing a finding about a known subject, so topic は is natural.

contrast_examples.jp: 密度が高い患者がいる。
contrast_examples.en: There's a patient whose density is high (new info).

prompt.context_jp: 「骨粗しょう症であった可能性___極めて低く」
prompt.prompt_jp: 骨粗しょう症であった可能性___極めて低く

feedback.correct_en: は topicalizes '可能性' — 'as for the possibility of osteoporosis, it is extremely low.' This is a judgment/evaluation of a known concept.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be odd — the possibility isn't newly introduced, it's being evaluated.

prompt.context_jp: 「曽根さん___は 他の病気が 潜んでいる可能性があります」
prompt.prompt_jp: 曽根さん___は、他の病気が潜んでいる可能性があります。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 曽根さん.

feedback.correct_en: に marks the location/person where the illness lurks — 'in/with Ms. Sone, there may be another illness hidden.' には adds topic focus.
feedback.incorrect_en: を/で don't fit; 潜んでいる takes に for the location where something lies hidden.

prompt.context_jp: 「そして 何より 技師の腕___重要なんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 技師の腕___重要なんです。

feedback.correct_en: が marks 技師の腕 as the exhaustive/identifying focus — 'what matters most is the technician's skill.' The 何より ('above all') cues exhaustive listing.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would weaken the emphasis; the speaker is singling out this one thing as THE important factor.

contrast_examples.jp: 大事なのは腕が重要だ。

contrast_examples.en: Skill is important (one of many things).

prompt.context_jp: 「技師の腕に 違いなんてあるとは思えません」「違い___あります」
prompt.prompt_jp: 違い___あります。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that answers back forcefully.

feedback.correct_en: 違いなら picks up Mutou's word '違い' contrastively — 'If you're talking about differences, there ARE some.' This is a pointed rebuttal.
feedback.incorrect_en: 違いがあります would be a flat statement; the story uses なら to echo and rebut the opponent's word.

contrast_examples.en: If it's time (you're asking about), I have some.

prompt.context_jp: 「心臓の冠動脈が こっち___ぼけていて こっち___鮮明に写ってるのが分かる」
prompt.prompt_jp: こっち___ぼけていて、こっち___鮮明に写ってる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the contrast between the two images?

feedback.correct_en: は marks contrastive topics — 'this one is blurry, (but) this one is clear.' This parallel は…は… pattern highlights the contrast between the two photos.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make each a new-information subject with no contrast relationship.

contrast_examples.jp: これは安く、あれは高い。
contrast_examples.en: This is cheap, that is expensive (contrast).
This one is the cheap one (identification).

prompt.context_jp: 「武藤さん___何のために戦ってるんですか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 武藤さん___何のために戦ってるんですか？

feedback.correct_en: は topicalizes 武藤さん — 'As for you, Mr. Mutou, what are you fighting for?' The speaker addresses him as a known topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it 'Who is fighting? Mutou!' — an identification question that doesn't match the context.

contrast_examples.jp: あなたは何を考えてる？

prompt.context_jp: 「真実を明らかにして 曽根さんを救いたい 目的___同じはずです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 目的___同じはずです。

feedback.correct_en: は topicalizes 目的 — 'as for the goal, it should be the same.' This frames a shared known concept being evaluated.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as newly introduced identification, which doesn't fit 'our goal is surely the same.'

prompt.context_jp: 「曽根さんには 他の病気の可能性___あるんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 他の病気の可能性___あるんです。

feedback.correct_en: が marks the newly presented fact — 'there IS a possibility of another illness.' This is new, urgent information An is revealing.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would background the information as known/topical, undermining the urgency of the revelation.

prompt.context_jp: 「たった今 救急搬送の 受け入れの要請___入りました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 受け入れの要請___入りました。

feedback.correct_en: が marks the sudden new event — a request just came in. Announcement-of-new-event sentences take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat the request as a known topic, which clashes with 'just now came in.'

contrast_examples.en: A phone call came in (new event).

prompt.context_jp: 「頭頸部に異常___ありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 頭頸部に異常___ありません。

feedback.correct_en: In negative existential statements ('there is no X'), は is natural: 異常はありません signals 'as for abnormalities, there are none.' A conventional medical finding pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: 異常がありません sounds unidiomatic; Japanese typically shifts to は under negation of existence.

prompt.context_jp: 「救急車___到着しました！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 救急車___到着しました！

feedback.correct_en: が announces a new, perceptible event — the ambulance has just arrived. Arrival announcements use が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the ambulance is a known topic being described, losing the urgency of the announcement.

prompt.context_jp: 「辻村先生___何も悪くありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 辻村先生___何も悪くありません。

feedback.correct_en: は topicalizes Dr. Tsujimura — 'as for Dr. Tsujimura, he is not at fault at all.' A reassuring statement about a known person.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would identify who is not at fault (Dr. T, not someone else) — possible but doesn't match the comforting tone.

contrast_examples.en: He is the one to blame (identification).

prompt.context_jp: 「あいつら 敵だなんて 思っちゃいねえんだよ」の後に続く問いで、「お前だって そうだろ？」の前の文脈：「彼は 敵___味方と考えている」(synthetic)
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼は敵___味方と考えている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks '敵' as the object of consideration?

feedback.correct_en: 〜を〜と考える/思う uses を to mark what is being regarded (as something). 'He regards enemies AS allies.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a subject; に doesn't fit the 〜を〜と pattern.

contrast_examples.en: I think of him as a friend.

prompt.context_jp: 「2000枚のＤＶＤの中から___正真正銘の曽根さんのデータです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 2000枚のＤＶＤの中から___正真正銘のデータです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that best fits the technicians' effort.

feedback.correct_en: 探し出す ('search out, hunt down') emphasizes the painstaking effort of locating data among 2000 DVDs — matching the technicians' pride.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見つけた is too neutral/accidental; 作った ('made') is factually wrong — they found existing data, not created it.

prompt.context_jp: 「うちなら 18時からできますから」「___残業しますよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___残業しますよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the expression that shows willingness.

feedback.correct_en: 喜んで ('gladly') conveys enthusiastic willingness — the team is eager to work overtime for the patient.
feedback.incorrect_en: 仕方なく ('reluctantly') contradicts the supportive tone; やっと ('finally') doesn't fit this future-tense offer.

contrast_examples.jp: 喜んでお手伝いします。

prompt.context_jp: 「敵であるあなたたちに ___わけにはいきません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 敵であるあなたたちに___わけにはいきません。

feedback.correct_en: 〜に任せる ('entrust to ~') fits: 'I can't leave it (the exam) to my enemy.' 任せるわけにはいきません is a natural refusal pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: 預かる means 'receive and keep (for someone)' — wrong direction. 頼る ('rely on') doesn't take わけにはいかない with this nuance here.

prompt.context_jp: 「間違いありません 曽根さんは 悪性リンパ腫です」の前の判断文：「造影ＣＴでは仙骨に対して 骨梁を保った___を示しています」
prompt.prompt_jp: 骨梁を保った___を示しています。

feedback.correct_en: 浸潤 ('infiltration') is the correct term for how malignant lymphoma spreads into bone while preserving trabeculae — a diagnostic hallmark.
feedback.incorrect_en: 骨折 means 'fracture' (the symptom, not the finding on CT). 変色 ('discoloration') is not a radiological descriptor used here.

contrast_examples.jp: 腫瘍の浸潤が見られる。

prompt.context_jp: 「幸い 病変は___していて 化学療法や放射線治療で根治も望めます」
prompt.prompt_jp: 病変は___していて、治療で根治も望めます。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word meaning 'confined to one area'.

feedback.correct_en: 限局 ('localized') is a medical term — the lesion is confined to one area, making curative treatment possible.
feedback.incorrect_en: 拡散 ('spread') would mean the opposite (bad prognosis). 悪化 ('worsening') doesn't fit 'treatment can cure it.'

prompt.context_jp: 「___ 自分が最も憎んでいた人たちと 同じことをするところでした」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___、同じことをするところでした。

feedback.correct_en: 危うく〜するところだった means 'I nearly/almost did ~ (dangerously close).' It perfectly captures Mutou's confession of nearly repeating what he hated.
feedback.incorrect_en: 幸いに means 'fortunately' — opposite tone. もちろん ('of course') doesn't collocate with するところでした.

contrast_examples.jp: 危うく転ぶところだった。

prompt.context_jp: 「___したよ 自分の未熟さを」
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分の未熟さを___した。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'feel keenly / painfully realize'.

feedback.correct_en: 痛感する ('feel painfully/acutely') fits Tsujimura's remorseful acknowledgment of his own inexperience.
feedback.incorrect_en: 満足 ('satisfaction') and 安心 ('relief') contradict the regretful tone.

contrast_examples.en: I feel the weight of responsibility keenly.

prompt.context_jp: 「実は 救急科に ___ことになりました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 救急科に___ことになりました。

feedback.correct_en: 転科する means 'transfer to a different (medical) department' within the same hospital — exactly what Tsujimura is announcing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 転職する is changing jobs (different employer); 転校する is changing schools — neither fits an in-hospital department move.

contrast_examples.jp: 外科から救急科に転科する。

prompt.context_jp: 「得意げな表情の裏に、___職人の誇りがのぞく」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___職人の誇りがのぞく。

feedback.correct_en: 譲れぬ ('cannot yield/compromise') captures Tanaka's unwavering craftsman pride — a core value he won't concede.
feedback.incorrect_en: 忘れた ('forgotten') or 失った ('lost') would mean the pride is gone — opposite of showing through.

prompt.context_jp: Tanaka is forcefully revealing the difference in technician skill after showing the two photos.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural and forceful in this climactic reveal?

choices.text: それは腕の違いなんです。

feedback.correct_en: それが…です！ with が makes the pronoun 'that' the exhaustive identifier — 'THAT (right there) is the difference in skill!' — punchy and triumphant.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) with は softens to a mere explanation; (c) is awkward word order that buries the punch of 'that's it!'

prompt.context_jp: Igarashi is pleading with Mutou to let them perform the exam.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is most natural as a sincere, polite plea?

choices.text: お願いです 僕たちに検査をさせてください
お願い 検査をしたい
検査をしてもいいですか

feedback.correct_en: お願いです + causative-request 〜させてください is the standard sincere plea: 'please let us do the exam.' It fits the stakes of the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is too casual for this tense professional moment; (c) asks permission to do something to the listener, which doesn't match asking to be allowed to examine the patient.

prompt.context_jp: Asked how long the exam will take, Igarashi gives a confident, committed answer.
prompt.prompt_en: Which response sounds most decisive and natural?

feedback.correct_en: 終わらせます (causative) shows the speaker's commitment to MAKE it end in 30 minutes — taking responsibility. Matches the urgency of the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: 終わります is a neutral prediction with no agency; かかるかも is vague, undermining the needed confidence.

contrast_examples.jp: 今日中に終わらせます。
contrast_examples.en: I'll get it finished by today.

prompt.context_jp: Tsujimura concedes to Igarashi after the case.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as a rueful admission between peers?

choices.text: やはり 君には勝てそうにないな
やはり 君に勝つことができません
君に勝てないと思います

feedback.correct_en: 勝てそうにないな with final な is a reflective, slightly resigned male-speech line fitting a senior conceding to a rival — natural in this personal moment.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is overly formal/stiff; (c) sounds like a flat statement of opinion, missing the rueful, in-the-moment realization.

contrast_examples.jp: 追いつけそうにないな。
contrast_examples.en: Doesn't look like I can catch up.

contrast_examples.jp: 追いつけないと思います。
contrast_examples.en: I don't think I can catch up (formal/flat).

prompt.context_jp: The narrator describes what a rival (as opposed to an enemy) is like.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for describing rivals who push each other to grow?

choices.text: お互いを認め合い 高め合う
お互いに認めて 高くする

feedback.correct_en: 認め合う・高め合う use the reciprocal 〜合う suffix, the idiomatic way to express mutual recognition and mutual elevation between rivals.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) uses the wrong verbs (高くする = make tall/raise price-like); (c) 認識する・上げる are literal but miss the mutual nuance.
